# Lewis Zhang — Co-Founder / CTO, Probook ## Scope and evidence limits This profile is limited to professionally public, non-sensitive information available as of 2026-08-27. I omitted sensitive material covered by the requested compliance exclusions; no omitted sensitive details are repeated here. Where the public record does not establish a fact, I mark it NOT FOUND rather than infer it. ## 1. Identity confirmation - Probook’s own company page names “Lewis Zhang” as “Co-Founder & CTO.” Quote: “Lewis Zhang — Co-Founder & CTO.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/company
- The subject’s LinkedIn profile identifies “Lewis Z.” as “Co-Founder CTO at Probook.” Quote: “Co-Founder & CTO at Probook.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- LinkedIn’s indexed employment record dates the Probook role “Jan 2024 - Present.” Quote: “Co-Founder CTO - Probook (Current) Jan 2024 - Present.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Probook’s investor, Sequoia, independently identifies “Lewis Zhang” as a Probook co-founder. Quote: “he and co-founders Lewis Zhang and Ben Cervantez launched Probook.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- A June 23, 2026 financing report also identifies the leadership team. Quote: “Led by Co-founders George Eliadis (CEO), Ben Cervantez, and Lewis Zhang.” URL: https://www.finsmes.com/2026/06/probook-raises-40m-in-seed-and-series-a-financing.html Same-name/similar-name people encountered and discarded:
- Lewis Zhang, LinkedIn URL https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisz — discarded because the indexed profile says “Investment Banking Associate” at Bank of America and previously CLSA, with University of Hong Kong and Columbia Business School; that does not match the target’s Probook/Roblox/UC Berkeley EECS history. Quote: “Investment Banking Associate — Bank of America” and “Investment Banking Associate — CLSA.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisz
- Zheyuan Zhang — discarded as a different person, not the target Lewis Zhang. The publication result lists the author as “Zheyuan Zhang.” Quote: “AUTHOR: Zheyuan Zhang.” URL: https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.112.pdf
- “Lewis” Zhang references in papers about the “Lewis signaling game” were not attributed to this person and were excluded. For example, the AAAI result lists authors “Qi Zhang, Richard Lewis, Satinder Singh, & Edmund Durfee,” not Lewis Zhang. Quote: “Zhang, Q., Lewis, R., Singh, S., & Durfee, E.” URL: https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/4525 ## 2. Career ### Probook
- Organisation/title: Probook — Co-Founder & CTO.
- Dates: January 2024–present, according to the indexed LinkedIn record. Quote: “Co-Founder CTO - Probook (Current) Jan 2024 - Present.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Responsibilities: NOT FOUND as a person-specific formal job description. Publicly documented company scope includes “dispatch,” “intake,” and “automating from intake to dispatch and beyond.” Quote: “built around dispatch ... automating from intake to dispatch and beyond.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- Publicly evidenced technical/product building: Probook describes itself as “the AI Operating System for Home Services,” and says its platform is built around dispatch. Quote: “Probook — The AI Operating System for Home Services.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/company
- Outbound sales, demand generation, ABM, target-account list building, or sales-development GTM tooling owned personally by Zhang: NOT FOUND. The company page only says, at team level, “Our GTM and CS teams came up at Procore, Zocdoc, and other vertical leaders.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/company ### Roblox
- Organisation/title: Roblox — Senior ML Engineer.
- Dates: January 2021–January 2024. Quote: “Senior ML Engineer - Roblox” and “Jan 2021 - Jan 2024.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Responsibility specifically reported by Sequoia: work on “the critical player-server matching team.” Quote: “was part of the critical player-server matching team at Roblox.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- Sales/GTM responsibility: NOT FOUND. ### Internships and research
The following dates and titles come from the indexed LinkedIn profile; the snippets do not provide complete responsibility descriptions for every role. - Confluent — Software Engineer Intern, March–May 2021. Quote: “Software Engineer Intern - Confluent ... Mar 2021 - May 2021.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Rubrik, Inc. — Software Engineer Intern, December 2020–March 2021. Quote: “Software Engineer Intern - Rubrik, Inc. ... Dec 2020 - Mar 2021.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Tesla — Software Engineer Intern, August–October 2020. Quote: “Software Engineer Intern - Tesla ... Aug 2020 - Oct 2020.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Intel Corporation — Software Engineer Intern, May–August 2020. Quote: “Software Engineer Intern - Intel Corporation ... May 2020 - Aug 2020.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Research — Research Intern, August 2019–May 2020. The indexed profile says he worked in Professor Trevor Darrell’s lab on Scalabel.ai. Quote: “Worked in Professor Trevor Darrell's lab, contributing to open source project Scalabel.ai, a web annotation tool for autonomous driving datasets.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Stanford University — Research Intern, June 2018–August 2019. The indexed profile says he developed a neural-network simulation model concerning grant-funding policy. Quote: “Developed a deep neural network simulation model with Professor Jay Bhattacharya ... to discover optimal policies for grant funding allocation.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Any outbound-sales, demand-generation, ABM, target-account-list, or sales-development tooling responsibility in these roles: NOT FOUND. ## 3. Education - University of California, Berkeley — Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Computer Sciences (EECS). The indexed profile lists “Bachelor of Science, EECS at University of California, Berkeley.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Probook says he completed Berkeley EECS in two years with a 4.0. Quote: “Lewis breezed through Berkeley EECS in two years with a 4.0.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/company
- Sequoia likewise says he “earned degrees in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from Berkeley in two years.” Quote: “earned degrees in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science from Berkeley in two years.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- Bellarmine College Preparatory — the indexed profile lists “Bellarmine College Preparatory” with “2019,” but does not state a credential. Quote: “Bellarmine College Preparatory ... 2019.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Post-graduate professional programmes: NOT FOUND. ## 4. Public writing, talks and podcasts Publicly attributable items found: - LinkedIn post, “I'm certainly not the best writer (way better at math) but I am going to start to be more active on LinkedIn and share the small wins,” LinkedIn, October 23, 2025. Quote: “I'm certainly not the best writer (way better at math) but I am going to start to be more active on LinkedIn and share the small wins.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/lewisfzhang_im-certainly-not-the-best-writer-way-better-activity-7387118180609085442-UJ-d
- LinkedIn post by Zachary Stack describing joining Probook after a call with Lewis, June 23, 2026. This is not authored by Zhang, but is a public reference to a conversation with him. Quote: “A year ago, I got a calendar invite for a 15-minute call with a founder named Lewis Z.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/zachary-stack-_a-year-ago-i-got-a-calendar-invite-for-a-activity-7475210012257255425-_PV3
- First-person articles, bylines, webinars, panels, podcasts, and conference talks by Lewis Zhang: NOT FOUND in the searched public results. Most substantive attributable quote found: “I'm certainly not the best writer (way better at math) but I am going to start to be more active on LinkedIn and share the small wins.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/lewisfzhang_im-certainly-not-the-best-writer-way-better-activity-7387118180609085442-UJ-d ## 5. What they own at Probook today - Title and broad ownership: Co-Founder & CTO. Quote: “Lewis Zhang — Co-Founder & CTO.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/company
- Product/technical domain publicly associated with Probook: an AI operating system for home-services businesses, centered on dispatch and connected customer context. Quote: “a single platform that shares context across the entire customer experience, automating from intake to dispatch and beyond.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- Engineering organisation: Probook publicly lists engineering openings for “Software Engineer (Backend),” “Software Engineer (Machine Learning),” and “Software Engineer (Product).” Quote: “Software Engineer (Backend) ... Software Engineer (Machine Learning) ... Software Engineer (Product).” URL: https://www.probook.ai/careers
- Which open roles explicitly report to Lewis: NOT FOUND. The careers page lists roles but does not state reporting lines. URL: https://www.probook.ai/careers
- Who reports to Lewis: NOT FOUND. No public org chart or person-specific reporting list was found.
- Publicly stated hiring/technical ambition: Probook says its engineering team includes “multiple ICPC World Finalists and IMO Gold Medalists.” Quote: “Our engineering team includes multiple ICPC World Finalists and IMO Gold Medalists.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/company
- Publicly stated product ambition: “transforming the home services industry.” Quote: “focused on transforming the home services industry.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/careers ## 6. How they think and buy Direct evidence about Zhang’s software-evaluation or purchasing process, tools he has praised or criticised, procurement criteria, buying committee behavior, or advocated methodologies: NOT FOUND. Evidence about product philosophy from public company/investor material, which should not be over-attributed to Zhang personally:
- Probook emphasizes a unified context layer rather than disconnected tools. Quote: “a single platform that shares context across the entire customer experience.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- The company frames the problem around operational impact in the trades and “taking the drudgery out of their work.” Quote: “obsessed with taking the drudgery out of their work.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- Communication style evidence from Zhang himself is concise, self-deprecating, and oriented toward incremental results. Quote: “way better at math” and “share the small wins.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/lewisfzhang_im-certainly-not-the-best-writer-way-better-activity-7387118180609085442-UJ-d
- Stated metrics personally attributed to Zhang: NOT FOUND. Publicly reported Probook customer metrics exist, but are not attributed to Zhang in the located source. A third-party summary reports “~12% sales increase” and “~19% flip-rate increase,” but this is aggregator evidence and should not be treated as Zhang’s stated metric. Quote: “Reported average outcomes of ~12% sales increase and ~19% flip-rate increase.” URL: https://yespress.io/probook ## 7. Non-sensitive personal hooks - Early coding interest: Sequoia says “Lewis started coding when he was 7.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/
- Academic achievement: Probook says he had “a perfect score on the AMC 12” and completed Berkeley EECS “in two years with a 4.0.” URL: https://www.probook.ai/letter
- Open-source/research hook: his Berkeley research internship involved Scalabel.ai, described as “a web annotation tool for autonomous driving datasets.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
- Publicly stated hobbies, sports, volunteering, awards beyond the AMC 12 statement, side projects, and other non-sensitive interests: NOT FOUND. ## 8. Three grounded conversation openers 1. Exact hook: Scalabel.ai and autonomous-driving dataset tooling. Opener: “You worked in Trevor Darrell’s lab on Scalabel.ai, described as a web annotation tool for autonomous-driving datasets—what did that experience teach you about building reliable data workflows for Probook?” Evidence quote: “contributing to open source project Scalabel.ai, a web annotation tool for autonomous driving datasets.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang 2. Exact hook: Probook’s dispatch-centered product architecture. Opener: “Sequoia describes Probook as sharing context across the customer experience and automating from intake to dispatch and beyond—what was the hardest context boundary to eliminate?” Evidence quote: “a single platform that shares context across the entire customer experience, automating from intake to dispatch and beyond.” URL: https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-probook-ai-for-the-trades/ 3. Exact hook: Zhang’s stated intention to share incremental wins publicly. Opener: “You wrote that you planned to ‘share the small wins’—which recent Probook engineering win has changed your mind most about the product?” Evidence quote: “start to be more active on LinkedIn and share the small wins.” URL: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/lewisfzhang_im-certainly-not-the-best-writer-way-better-activity-7387118180609085442-UJ-d ## Source-quality note Primary/near-primary sources used include Probook’s company, careers, and letter pages; Zhang’s LinkedIn profile and post; and Sequoia’s partner article. LinkedIn details are indexed/profile evidence rather than independently verified employment records. RocketReach and YesPress are aggregators and were not used as the sole basis for identity; the indexed RocketReach snippet merely says “Lewis Zhang is the Co-Founder and CTO of Probook.” URL: https://rocketreach.co/probook-profile_b6d7dc12c74238a4

_request.query:
Produce an exhaustive, cited markdown profile of Lewis Zhang (Co-Founder / CTO at Probook):

1. IDENTITY CONFIRMATION — the primary sources that tie this exact person to Probook and this
   exact title, with dates. List the same-name people you excluded.
2. CAREER — every role with organisation, title and start/end dates, and what they were
   responsible for at each. Highlight anything to do with outbound sales, demand generation,
   account-based marketing, target-account list building, sales development or GTM tooling.
3. EDUCATION — institutions, degrees, dates, and any post-graduate or professional programmes.
4. PUBLIC WRITING, TALKS AND PODCASTS — every post, article, byline, webinar, panel or podcast
   appearance you can find, with title, venue, date and URL. Quote the most substantive one.
5. WHAT THEY OWN AT PROBOOK TODAY — scope of the role, who reports to them, which open Probook
   roles report into them, and what they have publicly said about what they are building.
6. HOW THEY THINK AND BUY — evidence about how they evaluate and purchase software: tools they
   have publicly praised or criticised, methodologies they advocate, their stated metrics, and
   their communication style (quote them).
7. NON-SENSITIVE PERSONAL HOOKS — publicly stated interests, hobbies, sports, schools, awards,
   volunteering, side projects. Nothing from the compliance exclusion list.
8. THREE GROUNDED CONVERSATION OPENERS — each must name the exact hook it uses and the URL that
   evidences it. No opener may rest on an unsourced fact.
_request.systemPrompt:
You are researching ONE named professional for a B2B buying-committee dossier.

TARGET LOCK — the ONLY subject is:
  Lewis Zhang, currently Co-Founder / CTO at Probook (probook.ai), the AI operating system for home-services
  businesses (plumbing / HVAC / electrical), headquartered in New York, NY.
  LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/lewisfzhang
  Known employment history (already verified, use it to disambiguate): Probook (co-founder & CTO, since 2024), Roblox (Senior ML Engineer, 2021–2024), internships at Confluent, Rubrik, Tesla and Intel; UC Berkeley EECS; Berkeley AI Research and Stanford research internships

Any person with the same or a similar name who does NOT match that employment history is a
DIFFERENT PERSON. Name every same-name person you encountered and discarded, and say why.

COMPLIANCE CHARTER — hard exclusions. Do NOT collect, report, quote or allude to: health or
medical information, religion or religious activity, political opinions or affiliation, sexual
orientation, racial or ethnic origin, trade-union membership, criminal matters, family or
bereavement details, home address, personal phone number or personal email address, or anything
about their children. If a source contains such material, skip it and say you skipped it. Only
professionally-public and clearly non-sensitive personal material is in scope.

RULES: every assertion carries a verbatim quote and its URL. Write "NOT FOUND" rather than
guessing. Prefer the person's own words (their posts, talks, interviews, bylines) over third-party
profiles. Aggregator/people-directory pages are the weakest evidence and must be labelled as such.

report.description: The exhaustive cited markdown profile answering every numbered section, with a verbatim quote and URL behind every assertion and explicit NOT FOUND markers.
